title: The life of a policy
summary: One policy from its manifest in chock-catalog, through chock compile and an install, to a tool call, its verdict and the decision log.
intro: A policy is written once, compiled into the files each surface runs, and installed per agent. After that, every tool call the agent makes runs through the hook, gets a verdict, and leaves one line in a local log.

boundaries.label: Build: once per policy, once per install
Each tool call, on your machine

nodes.label: Policy manifest
nodes.card: A policy is a folder under chock-catalog's base/. Its manifest.yaml names the policy, its enforcement and its hook: a declarative gate, or a guard script in implementations/. This one declares a content gate on commit and on tool use.

nodes.label: chock compile
nodes.card: Reads a policy folder and runs one emitter per surface: the ambient rule, agent hooks, git hook, CI step, Claude managed settings and the MCP gateway. The output lands in .chock/compiled/<policy>/.

nodes.label: gate.json
nodes.card: The manifest's hook.gate, resolved into one gate.json per surface: before a tool runs, at the turn's end, in the git hook and in CI.

nodes.label: Guard script
nodes.card: A policy's own program, for a check a pattern cannot express. The hook hands it the shell command (--guard) and reads its verdict. The cited one is block-destructive-commands.

nodes.label: Ambient rule
nodes.card: Text the agent reads, as an AGENTS.md block. It blocks nothing on its own; the gate and the guard do.

nodes.label: Install per agent
nodes.card: The chock sync command writes each agent's hook file in that agent's own format, and its runtime into .chock/bin/. The chock install command builds the same for one agent as a plugin (ask the user before running either). Each hook command names the gate.json or guard it runs.

nodes.label: A tool call
nodes.card: The agent's client runs the hook before the tool runs and passes the call on stdin. Agentseam's dispatcher reads it, and that agent's adapter turns the payload into one Event.

nodes.label: Verdict
nodes.card: Evaluates the compiled gate, caps the verdict by the rollout level in force, and concludes with an exit code: block, ask, warn or allow.

nodes.label: Back to the client
nodes.card: The adapter speaks the Decision in the client's own dialect, and the client refuses or runs the tool. What a hook can do in each agent, and what happens when it cannot run, is agentseam's data, not ours.

nodes.label: Decision log
nodes.card: One line per hook call, in a local file: <repo>/.chock/log/gate-events.jsonl on the repo route, ~/.chock/log/<agent>/events.jsonl on the plugin route. Writing it never changes the decision, and the hook sends nothing over the network.
